column8: The git connector binds an Intent: trailer only when it sits inside git's FINAL trailer block (kernel/internal/connector/git/SPEC.md: "Only a final Git trailer block may populate IntentTrailers"; INV-28 "subject/body mentions never create an intent_refs entry"). By the kernel grammar, 17 of the 30 commits carrying an Intent line have no bindable trailer (14 of them touched governed paths, so the gate demanded a trailer and was satisfied by a body line; 3 touched none) — including the release-line precedent 34af46d and the 2026-11-16 release-line commit a028984 — the Intent: line is a body paragraph separated from Co-Authored-By by a blank line, so proofbound intent check --commit prints intent=none and the Trust Record holds NO claim for them; the other 13 place it correctly and bind (verified: a5a085b resolves to records:CI-staged-pin-guard-7b3c9d@1673422f…). The shell gate scripts/intent-delivery-applicability.sh greps %B for ^Intent: anywhere, so make check is green either way: the harness verifies presence, not binding (Law 9 corollary — a verdict is only as good as its harness). The convention existed and drifted; it was never enforced. No history rewrite is proposed for the 17; they are a known tombstone. FIXED 2026-11-16 (CI-intent-trailer-block-xp2pke, BR-gate-integrity-4b2e08 O-1): the gate now ports the kernel intentTrailers grammar + resolution-time value rule; both parsers are pinned to one shared corpus (scripts/tests/fixtures/intent-trailers, 12 cases) by TestIntentTrailers_SharedCorpus and intent-delivery-applicability.test.sh, each with a demonstrated positive control; on real history the gate refuses a028984 and accepts a5a085b. Condition (3) CHANGED with reason: a live proofbound intent check inside make check needs embedded Postgres + a synced ledger, making the gate environment-dependent (forbidden by O-1); parser parity via the shared corpus replaces it. Status stays OPEN pending a non-author verdict on the gate change (Law 9; the author fixed it and may not accept it). column8: A change intent can never supersede an earlier revision of itself. kernel/internal/connector/intent/intent.go validates a change intent's targets, constrained_by, and supersedes as ONE list that must ascend strictly by key (source, record_kind, record_id, digest, relation); every change intent needs at least one target, targets are requirement references, and a supersedes reference to an earlier change-intent revision has record_kind change_intent, which sorts before requirement, so the combined list always descends and is rejected (intent: invalid reference). Requirements escape this only by luck (business_decision sorts before requirement). Found 2026-11-16 when extending CI-intent-trailer-block-xp2pke's scope; worked around with a NEW intent (CI-intent-trailer-range-gwi9uu). No change intent in the repository has a second revision, so this has never fired before. Kernel defect in the canonical model, not fixed: it changes intent-SPEC validation and needs its own spec amendment and non-author review.

column8: Pre-existing, found by R2 M3 review rounds 6-7: obligation_verdicts_view (kernel/internal/projections/projections.go reduceObligationVerdict) upserts on (verdict_id, requirement source/id/digest, obligation_id) and never updates commit_sha or the intent columns. So (a) a v2 verdict revision that changes only reviewed_commit moves its outcome onto the OLD commit's row (a NOT_SATISFIED rev1 for X1 then SATISFIED rev2 for X7 makes X1 pass and X7 never pass); (b) a revision that moves to a new requirement revision leaves the old rows' outcomes warranting the old commit; (c) reverting an artifact to byte-identical earlier content dedupes as existing (store key source/native_id/content_sha), so the later outcome stays. Reachable today with records claims; R2 M3 makes it reachable for sdd commits and changes none of it. Owner decision 2026-11-19: defer, fix separately (it changes how projections record verdicts).

column8: proofbound check lists only commits that carry an Intent: sdd:<name> claim (kernel/internal/cli/check.go classifiedRange); every other commit in base..HEAD is dropped silently. A PR with one reviewed claiming commit plus one PROOFBOUND_NO_INTENT=1 commit carrying unrelated code reads WARRANTED (1 of 1), even with --require-claims; a PR with no claims passes by default. The bundle's VERIFY.md names non-claiming commits but nothing fails. Also: the check only protects main when it is a required status check under branch protection, which QUICKSTART does not say. Found from code reading during the DEMO-MANUAL trial; not yet proven by a test. Long-term direction (not decided): judge the merged tree diff, not commits; each spec declares the paths it governs; every changed hunk is covered, exempt (docs, gates/, keys, review artifacts) or UNCOVERED, and any UNCOVERED hunk makes the PR NOT WARRANTED. RESOLVED 2026-11-22 at commit granularity (CI-mvp-uncovered-code-581081, CLI-INV-33): check lists every unclaimed commit that changes a non-housekeeping path as UNCOVERED and the PR is NOT WARRANTED; QUICKSTART section 4 says to make the check a required status check. column8: Today agents bind commits to specs only because the init-written AGENTS.md block (kernel/internal/cli/starterkit/agents-block.md) tells them to type Intent: sdd:<name> or PROOFBOUND_NO_INTENT=1: prose the agent must remember, and a scope the agent asserts about itself. Proofbound designs only for agent coding, so the binding should need no declaration and trust none. Options raised 2026-11-22, none decided: (1) derive the hunk-to-spec mapping from the diff against each spec's declared area, the claim becoming only a cross-check (shares the coverage model with DEF-CHECK-UNCLAIMED-CODE-001); (2) bind the task at agent session start (proofbound task start, or a SessionStart hook / MCP tool) and stamp the trailer with prepare-commit-msg; (3) Proofbound writes typed trailers for its own commits (review, keys, spec), each path-checked, retiring PROOFBOUND_NO_INTENT=1; (4) work with no spec means drafting and approving a spec change first, never an opt-out; (5) harness hooks (PreToolUse on Edit/Write) warn or refuse edits outside the active spec's area. Principle: everything in the agent's own environment is guidance and early feedback only; the trust boundary is the server-side derivation bound to the merged tree. Owner 2026-11-22: defer for later, for thorough consideration. 2026-11-22 minimal slice built (CI-mvp-agent-intent-3k7q2w, CLI-INV-34..36): proofbound task start|stop and the init-installed prepare-commit-msg / commit-msg hooks stamp and require the claim on code commits. Still open: options 1 (derived coverage), 4 (spec-first workflow), 5 (harness hooks), session ingest of the task.
